qt: to the Commission Siegbert Frank Droese (ESN) Subject:

In Germany, occupational pension schemes provide pensions for people working in the liberal professions (doctors, dentists, lawyers, etc.), although membership is often mandatory for them. Recently, several of these institutions come under criticism as they have made significant losses on investments and revealed possible shortcomings in risk management, monitoring and supervision. For example, the pension scheme of the Berlin Chamber of Dental Practitioners (VZB) has suffered considerable losses, and large losses have also been reported for other schemes, in particular in connection with real estate investments. In view of the recent significant losses in German occupational pension schemes, does the Commission see any regulatory gaps in the EU regulatory framework for pensions, in particular with regard to risk management, transparency and the monitoring of investments?
